cues.fragment: Through drought and famine, natural disasters
cues.title: Warm Chest-Voice Entry
cues.text: Start in a relaxed, conversational chest register (around F#3–A3); lean behind the bass beat with zero throat squeeze.

cues.fragment: Kingdoms have fallen, angels be calling
cues.title: Legato Sustain & Internal Rhymes
cues.text: Connect 'fallen' and 'calling' with 89% vowel sustain, keeping the jaw loose as the phrase settles into the low cadence.

cues.fragment: Every time I look into your eyes I see it
cues.title: Pre-Chorus Lift to E4
cues.text: Span 11 semitones cleanly up to E4 with natural vibrato (31%); let the vowel narrow slightly as the pitch rises.

cues.fragment: Every time I get a bit inside I feel it
cues.title: Agile Melodic Turn
cues.text: Highest agility line in Verse 1: articulate each descending step on 'inside I feel it' distinctly before the chorus.

cues.fragment: Oooooooh, who would've thought I'd get you
cues.title: Signature Falsetto Float (A4)
cues.text: Release into a pure, airy head-voice 'Oooooooh' up near A4 (90% sustain), then drop smoothly back into chest mix on 'get you'.

cues.fragment: Your cries they can be heard from far and wide
cues.title: Open Resonance on 'Far and Wide'
cues.text: Keep a tall, vertical 'ah' vowel on 'far and wide' so the upper-chest extension rings out without pushing volume.

cues.title: 93% Sustain Anchor
cues.text: Hold 'need' steady on a clean, straight-to-vibrato tone before resetting your breath for the second pre-chorus.

cues.fragment: Oooooooh, who would've thought I'd get you (Chorus 2)
cues.title: Longest Sustained Falsetto (95%)
cues.text: Meter your airflow with steady rib expansion so the high A4 'Oooooooh' floats effortlessly through the full bar.

cues.fragment: The memories, It's all just memories
cues.title: 19-Semitone Bridge Sweep & Vibrato
cues.text: Rich vibrato peak (36%): let the melody cascade across 19 semitones on 'memories' while keeping the larynx neutral.

cues.fragment: Don't you love when I come around
cues.title: Rhythmic Call-and-Response Pocket
cues.text: Use crisp forward consonants ('d', 'l', 'c') to lock the syncopated bridge groove right into the pocket.

cues.fragment: Oooooooh, who would've thought I'd get you (Chorus 3)
cues.title: Dynamic Climax into Final Chorus
cues.text: Strongest vocal presence of the track (82% strength): transition seamlessly from the bridge build into the soaring A4 hook.

cues.fragment: Just be my lover / Boy you'll lead me to paradise
cues.title: Kali Uchis Outro Float
cues.text: Widest interval span (20 semitones) with a light, breathy timbre; taper the final 'paradise' gently into silence.
